jobs.summary: Full Outline/Context draft from your interview notes: field notes, research question + reflection, sharper thesis options, 4 context paragraphs, paper outline, sources. Next: paste Dr. Wolf’s prompt to check the parts, add real quotes, rewrite in your voice. Due Tue 2:55 PM.

replies.text: find a better way to get the media.

My name is Dylan Riegert interviewing Scott Riegert, my father. It is October 12th, 2026. This is for UGA Hist2112, and the Oral history assignment. Scott was in his home office in atlanta, and I was in my apartment. The interview was friendly and conversational about the relative topics of digitization of media, and the effects that had on the work force and basic human interaction. I was definitely nervous to conduct such a lengthy interview, but I think that truly it went well and a lot of material of substance was produced.

Summary: 

Introduction and Childhood media;
Consent for interview and introduction as stated in field notes. My father has worked for CNN for 40 years, and has seen how media has directly impacted the global access to information. This includes the shift to colored television, vcr, radio, records, magazines, and newspapers. 
Personal media consumption continued:
My father would listen to the twins games(baseball) on the radio with his friends on the block corner and share radios. Additionally he would keep a smaller radio under his pillow and fall asleep listening to sports broadcasts as a kid. 

Additionally people would hear music on the radio, and it was more of an advertisement for records and physical sales. You’d hear a song and go down to the record store, ask to hear a song or album, and the worker would play it for you. Mr. Riegert went as far as to explain they’d take the plastic off the albums and play them brand new so customers could sample the albums. Usually, you’d like it and buy it, according to my father, but I wondered what would happen if they had to replace it on the rack as far as rewrapping, and if it showed scratches from use. 

Scott Riegert had a walkman with cassettes which represents the physical handheld device/media one had to carry on their person to listen to music. This later progressed to smaller discs and CDs. 

Question of the value of media 

I asked my father if people value media less now since they are not required to carry around physical objects or means to acquire said media (smartphones). Additionally I asked about availability of media potentially ruining the novelty of it.  The mass availability of media has without a doubt changed how we listen to and receive any form of media.

To the contrary, saving a large amount of songs in a playlist online is a great example of how technology has made our lives easier in this context. 

Growing up around media (my grandfather)
Scott’s father was a news anchor and DJ. At 12 years old my father was able to learn about the workings of a proper studio in California under the supervision of my grandfather Lou Waters. On set in San Diego, Mr. Riegert learned to shoot and splice real film. This is a great example of older methods of media, and there was a lot of great discourse surrounding the nature of older film manipulation and use. 

Another thing we discussed was the nature of older graphics for the show being made. 

Starting in media 
My dad started at CNN after dropping out of community college. His start was right around 1984. He went into great detail about the process of the business with this era’s tech as well as contrasted it with more present norms. 


Then versus now
We then discussed the major differences between when he was just starting versus how new technology changed his industry as well as the way people perceived media. 


2. 
Your central research question(s) and reflections on how the interview contributes (or fails to contribute) to your understanding of those questions. Update your historical context paragraphs to analyze how your narrator fits into it.


My central research question is how has digitization changed the way Americans access, own, collect, preserve, and share media such as music, films, photographs, books, games, news, and visual design?

This interview greatly increased my understanding of the progression that occurred with technology. This was someone’s first hand experience growing up with media becoming digitized, and his answered showed. 

Thesis statement:

Scott Riegert’s career at CNN, from being a teleprompter to head director, shows that the digitization of American media and news did not replace physical media with faster, more efficient means. 

It simply relocated labor and changed the means that american citizens acquire their media.
